To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
fifteen chiral derivatising reagents were synthesised on cyanuric chloride and their diastereomeric derivatives of five β-blocker drugs were resolved on C-18 column by HPLC.

fifteen chiral derivativizing reagents synthesized on a cyanuic chloride platform were used to prepare diastereomers of five β-blocker enantiomers, namely, atenolol, propranolol, bisoprolol, metoprolol and carvedilol.

the enantioresolution of β-blockers as their diastreomers prepared with CDRs synthesized on a cyanuryl chloride platform was achieved on a C( 18) column and the method was validated for accuracy and precision.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel and efficient method for the resolution of enantiomers of five β-blocker drugs using a simple and cost-effective method.
the development and validation of reversed-phase high-performance chromatography (RP-HPLC) method for enantioresolution of (R,S)-β-blockers.

synthesis of CDRs having amino acids or amino acids amides as chiroptical auxiliaries on the cyanuric chloride scaffold, their diastereomerization of five β-blocker enantiomers and their separation on a C(8) column using gradient elution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the enantiomeric resolution of the β-blockers by HPLC was achieved with all the fifteen CDRs synthesized.

the CDRs synthesized with amino acid amides are more efficient than those prepared with amino acids, and CDRs synthesized on the cyanuric chloride are better than those prepared on 6-methoxycyanuric chloride.
the enantioseparation efficiency of the reagents depends on the nature of the chiral auxiliary, i.e. amino acids, and their amides, in the CDR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the C(18) stationary phase is a suitable choice for separation of diastereomeric derivatives of the β-blockers, and the chiral amino acid amides are superior to amino acids in terms of separation efficiency.
the chiral auxiliary amino acid or amino acid amide plays the most important role in separation of the diastereomers.

the diastereomers of the five β-blockers were resolved on a C(19) column using the fifteen CDRs and the best results were obtained with CDR 13 and CDR 15 for (R)- and (S)-atenolol and CDR 14 for (R)-propranol, CDR 12 for (S)-propranol and CDR 13 for (R)-carvedil.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the amino acid amides as chelating groups are more efficient than amino acids in the CDR synthesis and the CDRs having chlorine substituents are better than those with methoxy substituents.
the CDRs synthesized on a cyanuic chloride platform can be used for the enantioresolution of β-blockers.
the chiral auxiliary amino acid or amino acid amide plays a more important role than the achiral substituants in the CDR.
